Subject: FathomPay — post-call: throughput/latency constraints & deployment readout

Alex — thanks for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps while it's fresh. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

Key pain points you shared:
- Real-time checkout scoring must hold P95 latency <= 120ms for 1k daily peak TPS spikes (burstable).
- Steady-state throughput target: ~100 concurrent requests (1.2M reqs/day) with 90% of requests < 30 token continuation.
- Cold-starts and model warmup on autoscale were causing 800–1,200ms tail latencies in your current infra.
- Data residency: payment data must stay in US-only infra; audit logs retained 7 years.

Goals we agreed on:
- Proof-of-concept: dedicated pool supporting 100tps sustained with 2x burst for seasonal spikes.
- P95 latency target for single-turn scoring <= 120ms, with exception handling and graceful fallback.
- Run a 2-week soak with canary traffic split after deployment.

Immediate next steps (action owners):
1) Redwood will produce a technical readout and topology recommendation (deliverable: ops workbook + cost estimate) — Karthik (by 09/02).
2) FathomPay to share required sample payloads, token length distributions, and security questionnaire answers — Alex / Priya (by 09/04).
3) Schedule a 60-minute deep tech workshop to validate kernel selection and burst plan — propose 09/06 or 09/07.

Attachments: draft MPA attached (fathompay-mpa-draft.pdf).

Thanks — I put Karthik and Grace on copy to provide the technical and CS follow-through.

—

Subject: RE: FathomPay — post-call: throughput/latency constraints & deployment readout

Alex / team — following Soojin's summary, attaching an ops workbook with the rapid topology proposal and cost bands (redwood-inference-proposal-ops.xlsx). Highlights below — happy to walk through in the workshop.

Short technical summary / recommendation:
- Model: recommend quantized open-llama-13b-quant (8-bit GPTQ) for a balance of throughput and output quality; validated on your sample transcripts (approx 24 token median continuation).
- Serving mode: Redwood Dedicated pool split across 2 availability zones (US-West1 + US-West2) with pinned instances to avoid cold-starts. Primary pool: 8 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state; secondary burst pool: autoscaling up to 16 GPUs for seasonal bursts.
- Inference config: continuous batching with dynamic batch size up to 16; aggressive KV cache reuse for multi-turn flows to drop per-token cost. Estimated steady throughput: 100–130 requests/sec depending on prompt length distribution.
- Latency expectation (P95): ~85–120ms on dedicated pool for single-turn scoring (our bench on similar payloads). Tail risk stems from network egress on cold replicas — mitigated by pre-warming + short-lived warm standby.
- Fallback plan: if model/variant unavailable, route to a smaller 7B quant variant with degraded scoring + a confidence flag. We recommend a canary routing policy (5% initial) and progressive rollout.

Security & compliance notes:
- Logs/audit: we will ship event-level audit logs to your S3 (US region) with SSE-KMS; retention policy parametized for 7-year retention.
- Data handling: no raw payment PANs will be persisted; summarized token. We can table this in the security questionnaire.

Cost/ops estimate (very rough):
- Baseline monthly (dedicated steady pool + 2-week canary): $68K–$85K depending on reserved term and quantization choices. Exact pricing in the workbook.

Deliverables I attached:
- redwood-inference-proposal-ops.xlsx (workbook: topology diagrams, perf numbers, cost bands, rollout checklist)

Requests for FathomPay before the workshop:
- Representative sample payloads (anonymized) and a 48-hour traffic trace if possible.
- Confirmation on maximum acceptable cold-fallback degradation and required SLA window for failover.

I'll be available for the workshop on 09/06 10:00–12:00 or 09/07 13:00–15:00 PT. Which works best?

—

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few notes from our side: 

- Confirmed: we'll anonymize and share a 72-hour traffic trace and example payloads by EOD 09/04. Priya will lead that.
- Workshop: 09/06 10:00 PT works for our infra and ML engineers. Please send a calendar invite.
- Procurement/legal: procurement@fathompay.com is looped to coordinate the MPA timeline; our procurement target is to sign within 30 days after the successful POC. They asked for a ballpark monthly number now for planning (the workbook helps).
- On fallback: acceptable to degrade to a 7B variant for up to 10% of requests, provided responses carry a confidence score and we can route higher-confidence requests back to the 13B pool.

I'll confirm once we upload traces. Also: for the security questionnaire, would you prefer we fill your standard form or send our internal SOC excerpts?
